Welcome to CSCU9E5: Software Engineering 1

Modules  

Key Contacts

British University Vietnam (BUV) | Autumn 2026

Welcome to Software Engineering 1! This module introduces you to the principles, processes, and practices involved in developing software systems, with a particular focus on requirements, analysis, design, and collaborative software development.

What is CSCU9E5 about?

CSCU9E5 introduces the fundamental concepts and practices of Software Engineering. Throughout this module, you will explore the following key topics:

  • Software engineering principles, development lifecycles, and team-working tools.

  • Version control and collaboration using Git and GitHub.

  • Requirements capture, analysis, and refinement.

  • Software modelling and specification, including state machines and hierarchical statecharts.

  • Legal, social, ethical, and professional concerns in software engineering.

Software engineering is about more than writing code. It involves understanding stakeholder needs, managing complexity, collaborating effectively, and designing software systems that meet their intended requirements.

This module focuses primarily on the early stages of the software development lifecycle, from requirements capture through to analysis, design, and specification. You will also gain practical experience using professional tools and techniques to support collaborative software engineering.

How is CSCU9E5 taught and how will I learn?

All scheduled teaching activities will take place face-to-face at British University Vietnam (BUV).

Lectures

Lectures take place once per week and introduce the key concepts, principles, and techniques covered in the module. You are expected to review the relevant learning materials on Canvas before attending each lecture.

Practical Labs

Practical labs take place each week and provide opportunities to apply the concepts introduced in lectures.

During these sessions, you will work on hands-on activities involving Git and GitHub, requirements analysis, software modelling, and statecharts. You will also develop practical skills in using tools such as Visual Studio Code, Markdown, Mermaid, and clj-statecharts.

Group Work and Collaboration

An important component of this module is collaborative software engineering. You will work in a small team to complete software engineering tasks, practise version control, communicate effectively, and develop shared project artefacts.

You will also have opportunities to demonstrate your individual understanding and practical skills.

How can I succeed in this module?

To make the most of your learning experience, you are encouraged to:

  • Review the weekly learning materials on Canvas before attending lectures.

  • Attend and actively participate in all lectures and practical labs.

  • Complete the practical activities and regularly practise using the software engineering tools introduced in class.

  • Communicate effectively with your teammates and contribute actively to group activities.

  • Ask questions, seek feedback, and engage with your lecturer whenever you need support.

Remember: Software engineering is not just about writing code. It is about understanding problems, designing appropriate solutions, and working effectively with others to develop reliable software systems.

We look forward to working with you throughout the module!
